fish.name: Silverling Dace
fish.flavor: Flashes through the riffles like loose change. The river is full of it, and yet somehow nobody feels rich.

fish.name: Bridgepost Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Loiters at the foot of the bridge pilings like it's waiting for someone. It has been waiting roughly six hundred years.

fish.name: Riffle Sculpin
fish.flavor: Grips the cobbles with its fins while the rapids roar overhead. Has never once been swept away, and will absolutely tell you about it.

fish.name: Millrace Minnow
fish.flavor: Rides the millrace down and turns up back at the top by lunch. Nobody knows the route. Nobody has asked.

fish.name: Pebblebelly Loach
fish.flavor: Swallows pebbles to hold its place in the current. On calm nights it rattles softly, like a maraca with opinions.

fish.name: Wader's Chub
fish.flavor: Follows anglers' boots around the shallows, gobbling whatever gets kicked loose. Locals consider it a colleague.

fish.name: Towpath Barbel
fish.flavor: Noses along the bottom like an old horse on the towpath: going nowhere in particular, but going there with dignity.

fish.name: Skimming Bleak
fish.flavor: Sips mayflies off the surface with an urgency that suggests it knows exactly how short life is. It does. The mayflies told it.

fish.name: Freckled Grayling
fish.flavor: Raises its great sail fin in fast water like a tiny ship tacking upstream. Smells faintly, inexplicably, of thyme.

fish.name: Cobblestone Bullhead
fish.flavor: Lives under a flat stone and answers the door for no one. Bites anyway, out of principle.

fish.name: Washerwoman's Roach
fish.flavor: Gathers where laundry was once beaten on the rocks, still hoping for crumbs from a workers' lunch three generations gone. Loyalty like that deserves a sandwich.

fish.name: Ha'penny Smelt
fish.flavor: Worth half a penny at market, which the smelt takes as an insult and the penny takes as a compliment.

fish.name: Rustnail Perch
fish.flavor: Strikes at anything that glints, which downstream of the old forge means a diet of mostly nails. Its dentist has given up.

fish.name: Bankside Ruffe
fish.flavor: Small, prickly, and first to every bait, like the neighbor who arrives early to the potluck specifically to complain about it.

fish.name: Stonepocket Darter
fish.flavor: Tucks itself into gaps between the stones like a letter into an envelope. Delivery perpetually pending.

fish.name: Sunday Trout
fish.flavor: Only bites on its day of rest, which it observes by doing exactly what it does every other day, but smugly.

fish.name: Ribbonwake Ide
fish.flavor: Leaves a wake like a ribbon pulled off a parcel. Anglers cast to the ribbon; the ide, by then, is elsewhere.

fish.name: Bargeman's Bream
fish.flavor: Follows the barges from lock to lock for spilled grain. Knows the shipping schedule better than the bargemen, who have quietly started consulting it.

fish.name: Two-Bridge Pike
fish.flavor: Patrols exactly the stretch between the old bridge and the new one. Neither bank has jurisdiction there, and it knows this.

fish.name: Kingfisher's Rival
fish.flavor: So quick that the local kingfisher gave up hunting it years ago. Now they just watch each other across the water with grudging professional respect.

fish.name: Raincaller Trout
fish.flavor: Rises only when rain is an hour out. The farmers watch it more closely than the sky, and the sky resents it.

fish.name: Lockkeeper's Tench
fish.flavor: Dozes in the lock chamber between openings. The lockkeeper leaves the gate a crack ajar for it, and both of them deny this.

fish.name: Weirsong Eel
fish.flavor: On still nights the weir hums a single low note. That is not the weir.

fish.name: Ladderleap Salmon
fish.flavor: Takes the weir in one leap and the compliments in stride. Comes back every year, mostly for the applause.

fish.name: Foamchaser Asp
fish.flavor: Hunts in the white water below the rapids, striking clean through the foam. Considers calm pools a retirement it hasn't earned yet.

fish.name: Miller's Thumb
fish.flavor: Flat-headed and unbothered, named for the old miller who pressed his thumb into every sack of flour. The fish presses its whole self into everything.

fish.name: Moonwake Grayling
fish.flavor: Its sail fin catches moonlight the way canvas catches wind. On the right night you can watch a little silver ship beat upstream against everything.

fish.name: Lamplighter Catfish
fish.flavor: Trails a soft glow along the riverbed at dusk, pausing beneath each bridge as if lighting it. The town stopped paying a lamplighter in 1904. The bridges stayed lit.

fish.name: Bridgetroll Burbot
fish.flavor: Squats beneath the old footbridge, ancient and unimpressed, asking every passing fish a riddle. The riddle is 'can I eat you.'

fish.name: Seamstress Loach
fish.flavor: Stitches back and forth across the shallows at dawn, mending the night's torn current. The river never thanks her. The river never has to.

fish.name: Floodmark Trout
fish.flavor: Appears only when the river runs above the old floodmark. Its spots record every flood since the mill drowned, and there is room on it for more.

fish.name: Tinker's Blade
fish.flavor: Thin as a knife the tinker forgot to sell and twice as sharp. Cuts upstream through the current, which pretends not to mind.

fish.name: Whirlpool Widow
fish.flavor: Circles the weir pool in slow mourning veils. Whatever she lost down there, she has never stopped looking, and she does not care for company.

fish.name: Toll-Taker of Nine Arches
fish.flavor: The great armored barbel beneath the ninth arch has collected a toll since before the bridge had a name: one shiny thing, no exceptions. The bridge, it should be noted, was paid off centuries ago.

fish.name: Undertow Shepherd
fish.flavor: Herds the drowned things downstream to wherever drowned things go. Anglers who hook it all report the same dream afterward: green water, a crook of silver, and the gentle feeling of being counted.

fish.name: The Silver Procession
fish.flavor: One fish that moves like a hundred, filing beneath the old bridge on certain evenings — a funeral or a festival, depending on the light. It has never once arrived anywhere.

fish.name: The Drowned Fiddler
fish.flavor: They say a fiddler fell from the bridge at his own wedding, still playing. Hook this fish and your line hums a reel no one alive remembers learning — and everyone, somehow, can dance to.

fish.name: Old Kingsilver
fish.flavor: The first salmon, they say — the one who leapt the falls before the falls had settled on a height. Every silver flash in this river is one of his grandchildren, and every angler's tall tale is about the day he almost stayed caught.

fish.name: The Weirmother
fish.flavor: She has lain below the weir so long the river bends politely around her. In dry summers the whole town walks down to the bank, quietly, to make sure she is still there. She always is. So far.

fish.name: The Silver Thread
fish.flavor: The river, it turns out, is woven, and this is the thread. Reel gently: every loose end from the mountain to the sea is watching you.
